---
title: "Best Practices"
---

::: {.stage}
[1 · Prototyping and debugging]{.stage-label}

- **Before submitting a job to LISSY**, use the **sample files** to prototype your code and debug it locally in advance.

- **If your prototype does not run as expected**, fix it locally first. Do not draw conclusions from the sample files: they are artificial and exist for instructional and debugging purposes only.
:::

::: {.stage}
[2 · Importing the data]{.stage-label}

- **Select only the variables needed** for your analysis.

- **Import conservatively.** When working with many country-year datasets, split the workload into several jobs and import a group of countries in each one, rather than combining as many datasets as possible in a single run.
:::

::: {.stage}
[3 · Writing the queries]{.stage-label}

- **Break statistical queries into several smaller jobs.** Queries that generate very large outputs can cause system congestion.

- **Do not attempt to view, examine, or print individual records at either the person or household level.** Certain program syntax and commands will trigger system security alerts and may interrupt traffic.

- **Do not use commands that violate our security measures.** More on this in the [FAQs](/faqs/index.html#forbidden-words).

- **Do not request frequencies on continuous variables**, as this tends to violate our security measures.
:::

::: {.stage}
[4 · Waiting for the output]{.stage-label}

- **Send each job only once.** If it is not returned, do not send it again.

- **Wait for each job to be returned** before submitting your next one.
:::

::: {.stage}
[5 · Plotting]{.stage-label}

- To create **multiple charts** in a single job run, name them differently. More on this topic in the following links for [Stata](/stata-users/tidy_plots.html) and [R](/r-users/tidy_plots.html).
:::
